domain: AI Governance / Technology Ethics / Risk Assessment
topic_summary: Analysis of the structural divide between existential AI risk (catastrophic/extinction scenarios from advanced AI) and near-term AI harms (present discrimination, misinformation, labor displacement). Research reveals an 83.1% in-group collaboration rate, separate institutional homes, and contested resource allocation, but recent generative AI advances are forcing epistemological convergence.

key_entities: Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) - foundational existential risk research org, founded by Eliezer Yudkowsky
Open Philanthropy - largest funder in existential risk space, backed by Dustin Moskovitz/Cari Tuna
Future of Life Institute - existential risk advocacy organization
AI Ethics community - distributed network focused on present harms, bias audits, sociotechnical analysis
Effective Altruism movement - philanthropic framework prioritizing tractable high-impact causes including AI x-risk
Workday AI discrimination plaintiffs (Mobley case) - concrete near-term harm victims
Elon Musk, Stephen Hawking, Nick Bostrom - public existential risk advocates
Federal funding agencies - limited appetite for alignment research
ML researcher community - median 5% p(extinction from AGI), higher concern for immediate harms
Conference/publication networks - separate institutional homes (83.1% homophily)
Cross-field brokers - 5% of papers account for 85% of bridging links
Generative AI systems - forcing epistemological convergence
key_tensions: Existential risk framing vs near-term harms framing (control problem vs justice problem)
Resource allocation: speculative catastrophic risks vs demonstrated present harms
Institutional separation: 83.1% in-group collaboration, fragile brokerage
Methodological divide: adversarial red-teaming vs sociotechnical audits

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: AI alignment as the shared commitment that AI systems must be made safe/beneficial, with contested interpretation of what 'safe' means and for whom
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Epistemic authority grounded in disciplinary methodology (computer science/philosophy for x-risk, STS/critical theory for ethics) and funding gatekeepers (EA donors vs federal agencies)

readings.commitment: Alignment means preventing catastrophic loss of control over advanced AI systems; priority is existential safety
readings.authority_grounding: Computer science/decision theory; EA philanthropic funding; median ML researcher p(extinction)=5%
readings.expected_structural_delta: High ε on speculative future capabilities; victim set is 'all of humanity' (undifferentiated); beneficiary is long-term future; adversarial red-teaming methodology; resource flow to capability-focused research

readings.commitment: Alignment means preventing present discriminatory/extractive harms from deployed AI; priority is justice for marginalized populations
readings.authority_grounding: STS/critical theory; demonstrated harms (Mobley case, bias audits); researcher concern distribution (malicious use 11%, jobs 7% >> x-risk)
readings.expected_structural_delta: High ε on deployed system audits; victim set is specific marginalized groups (age, race, disability); beneficiary is present vulnerable populations; sociotechnical audit methodology; resource flow to bias mitigation

readings.commitment: Alignment requires addressing both catastrophic and present harms as complementary rather than competing priorities
readings.authority_grounding: Recent generative AI scholarship forcing epistemological convergence; recognition of false dichotomy
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate ε on both capability risks and deployment harms; victim set spans present marginalized groups AND future populations; dual methodology (red-teaming + audits); resource allocation balances both

axiom_contradictions.basis: Existential reading's axiom that undifferentiated future humanity is the primary victim set is incompatible with nearterm reading's axiom that present marginalized populations bear differentiated harms requiring prioritized redress. No single framework can simultaneously hold 'all future people equally' and 'present victims disproportionately' as the primary moral patient.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Multi-lens scan applied (network science, STS, moral philosophy, institutional economics). Dark matter probes surfaced broker fragility and federal funding absence. Kernel decomposition coherent: two readings with genuinely incompatible victim-set axioms, not merely different policy preferences.
